core_obligations: Set up the differential module over a suitable subring (proof lines 2356-2375): write A as a power series ring in two variables and L as the extension by a p-th root of an element f; since the differential of f is nonzero, choose a finite subextension of the coefficient field such that the differential stays nonzero over it, and observe that the relative differential module of A over the corresponding subring is finite free of rank e plus two, with a chosen top form.

Construct the comparison map and compute on a basis (proof lines 2377-2404): the trace gives a map on top relative differentials which by duality corresponds to a comparison map from the top relative differentials of B to the dualizing module of B; the claim that its cokernel is annihilated by a nonzero element is proved by exhibiting, for each index, an element of the top relative differentials of B whose image under the trace on the basis of the extension takes the value one on the matching basis element and zero on the others, which follows from the explicit description of the trace and from the nonvanishing of the chosen top form.

Transport along modifications and conclude (proof lines 2406-2436): for a normal modification of the spectrum of B one reduces as in the separable case to the situation where the modification is finite over a modification of the spectrum of A which is a sequence of blowups in closed points; applying the trace and the comparison lemma for such sequences produces a map on top relative differentials of the modification extending the previous comparison map, so the image of the global sections of the dualizing module of the modification contains the image of the comparison map; by the claim the cokernel is annihilated by a fixed nonzero element, and the bound criterion then gives that reduction to rational singularities is possible.
proof_roadmap: Choose a subring over which the defining element has nonzero differential, and record that the relative differential module is finite free of computable rank.
Show the cokernel of the comparison map built from the trace is annihilated by a nonzero element by computing on the power basis of the extension.
Reduce an arbitrary normal modification to a finite one over a sequence of point blowups, extend the comparison map along the modification, and apply the bound criterion.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a complete regular local ring of dimension two and characteristic p and a purely inseparable extension of its fraction field of degree p, the integral closure admits reduction to rational singularities (statement lines 2348-2354). The proof (proof lines 2356-2439) chooses a subring over which the defining element has nonzero differential, builds a comparison map from the trace of relative top differentials, proves that its cokernel is annihilated by a nonzero element through an explicit computation on the power basis of the extension, transports the comparison along modifications reduced to sequences of point blowups, and concludes by the bound criterion. H3: an original construction with explicit basis computations and a modification reduction, written out in full.
